title: Two walks, one shape
labels: Perimeter: the walk around the edge.
One shape. Two things to measure.
description: Three identical rectangles are displayed across two levels. On the upper left, a rectangle has a thick teal boundary and a white interior, with a dotted horizontal arrow pointing right above its top edge; below it, a card reads "Perimeter: the walk around the edge.". A vertical dashed line separates the upper shapes, labeled "different questions" reading upward. On the upper right, the rectangle has an amber fill and a thin grey boundary, above a card reading "Area: the covering inside.". Centered below, the rectangle combines both features with a thick teal boundary and amber fill, labeled "O...

title: One wire, three shapes
labels: Same wire. Different shapes. Same perimeter.
description: A blue wire with ticks marking 36 unit segments is labelled "36 cm of wire". A bracket beneath it connects via three arrows to three shapes: a square, an equilateral triangle, and a regular hexagon. All sides are labelled: four sides of "9" on the square, three of "12" on the triangle, and six of "6" on the hexagon. Underneath, boxes show "9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36", "12 + 12 + 12 = 36", and "6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 36". The bottom box reads "Same wire. Different shapes. Same perimeter.".

title: Straight and slanted
labels: One straight unit is called s. One slanted unit is called d. d is longer, so we never mix them.
description: A unit square with its straight side and its slanted line, the two lengths laid side by side so the slanted one is visibly longer, and a triangle on a dot grid written as 6s + 3d.

title: Edge and inside
labels: Perimeter = 16 units. We count steps along the edge.
Area = 15 square units. We count squares inside.
Different things. Different units. Never mix them.
description: A 5 by 3 rectangle drawn twice on a faint grid: on the left with its edge walked in teal in 16 steps, on the right with its inside filled by 15 amber squares, and below them one unit of length and one square unit.

title: Why squares win
labels: Same rectangle. Always the same answer.
A unit of area must tile with no gaps and no overlaps. Squares do. Circles do not.
description: The same rectangle filled with circles in rows (42), with circles packed another way (44), and with squares that leave no gaps, with the gaps between circles shaded to show the wasted space.

title: A Triangle and Its Rectangle
labels: Different-looking triangles. Same rectangle. Same area: half of it, every time.
description: Three rectangles of the same size, each holding an amber triangle labelled twelve, with the three triangles shaped differently. Under them a caption says the triangles look different but are the same half of the same rectangle, and a strip shows the rectangle with area twenty-four, the triangle with twelve and a half sign between them.

title: Charan's house plan
description: A floor plan of a house on a rectangular plot, 35 ft by 30 ft, with eight rooms each labelled with its measurements and area, three thin lines showing where rooms must share a measurement, and the total area in a box.
